### 1. Compare areas
The target consists of a \(5\times5\) rectangle and a \(3\times3\) extension, so

\[
A_{\text{target}}=25+9=34.
\]

The piece areas, in the same units, are

\[
A_1=13,\qquad A_2=13,\qquad A_3=21,\qquad A_4=23.
\]

Thus the only pairs whose areas total \(34\) are \(1+3\) and \(2+3\).

### 2. Test the possible placements
Place piece 3 toward the right of the target. The resulting division of the target is shown below, where each character represents one unit square and dots are outside the target:

\[
\begin{array}{llllllll}
2&2&2&3&3&.&.&.\\
2&2&3&3&3&.&.&.\\
2&2&2&3&3&3&3&3\\
2&2&3&3&3&3&3&3\\
2&2&2&3&3&3&3&3
\end{array}
\]

The uncovered region labeled \(2\) has row widths \(3,2,3,2,3\), exactly matching piece 2. Piece 1 instead has recesses of unequal heights, so it cannot match this remaining region.

Therefore, pieces 2 and 3 fit the target exactly.
